summary: The following AlloyDB AI features and improvements are generally available (GA): Smart batching for AI functions: AI function acceleration is generally available for ai.if, ai.rank, ai.analyze_sentiment, ai.summarize, ai.extract, ai.classify, and ai.generate on AlloyDB clusters running PostgreSQL 17 and later. Smart batching automatically batches and offloads eligible AI operations for asynchronous evaluation. It improves query execution speed without requiring you to rewrite queries into complex array structures. In PostgreSQL 18 and later, this feature is enabled by default. For more information, see Accelerate performance for queries with AI functions. Sentiment analysis: the ai.analyze_sentiment function is generally available on AlloyDB clusters running PostgreSQL 17 and later. This built-in function classifies the sentiment of text as positive, negative, or neutral directly within SQL queries in real time. For more information, see Analyze text sentiment.
title: The following AlloyDB AI features and improvements are generally available (GA): Smart batching for AI functions: AI function acceleration is generally available for ai.if, ai.rank, ai.analyze_sentiment, ai.summarize, ai.extract, ai.classify, and ai.generate on AlloyDB clusters running PostgreSQL 17 and later.

summary: You can now tune SQL queries using AI. Available starting with version 1.6.2 of the google_ml_integration extension, the ai.tune_sql function uses an LLM along with query execution plans, schemas, and runtime stats to recommend query optimizations. The function identifies performance bottlenecks and provides recommendations for query rewrites, indexes, statistics collection, Grand Unified Configuration (GUC) flags, and table analyze and vacuum operations. This feature is in Preview. For more information, see Tune SQL queries using AI and Database advisor flags.

summary: In response to GCP-2026-071, Google is updating AlloyDB managed components. The fix to the certificate store is shipped in a new maintenance version that AlloyDB applies during scheduled maintenance, so you don't need to manually update AlloyDB managed instances. You can also apply the fix by performing self-service maintenance. Depending on how you connect to AlloyDB, take the following actions: If you use the AlloyDB Auth Proxy, then upgrade it to v1.17.2 or later. If you run the standalone proxy binary, then also update the host's certificate authority (CA) certificates. If you use the AlloyDB Language Connectors, then update the language runtime and operating system CA certificates (for example, Go 1.26.10 or 1.27.3 or later).
title: In response to GCP-2026-071, Google is updating AlloyDB managed components.

title: AlloyDB provides more accurate memory usage estimation and prevents out-of-memory (OOM) errors when you build a ScaNN four-level tree index.

summary: Identity and Access Management (IAM) group authentication is generally available (GA) for new and existing AlloyDB clusters running PostgreSQL 15 and later. With IAM group authentication, you can manage database roles and privileges at the group level across primary instances and read pool instances, including first-time sign-ins directly to read pool instances. You can also preserve individual and IAM group user configurations when you migrate from a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL backup. For more information, see IAM database authentication overview and Manage IAM authentication.
title: Identity and Access Management (IAM) group authentication is generally available (GA) for new and existing AlloyDB clusters running PostgreSQL 15 and later.

label: GA
summary: The following AlloyDB AI and vector search features and improvements are generally available (GA): The alloydb_scann extension supports four-level tree (4LT) ScaNN vector indexes on PostgreSQL 17 and later, providing support for tables with up to 10 billion vector rows. For more information, see Four-level ScaNN tree indexes. 4LT ScaNN vector indexes support automatic index maintenance. For more information, see Create a ScaNN index and Maintain vector indexes automatically. You can enable streaming functionality for ScaNN vector indexes by setting the scann.satisfy_limit parameter to relaxed_order. When enabled, the vector scan continues searching through additional leaf partitions until it finds enough results to satisfy the LIMIT clause of your query, improving recall on filtered searches. Additionally, you can enable this feature for parallel process scans by setting the scann.enable_parallel_satisfy_limit database flag to on. For more information, see ScaNN index reference and Best practices for tuning ScaNN indexes. Vector assist simplifies the deployment and management of your AlloyDB vector workloads by helping you set up production-ready vector search capabilities, including embedding generation, query optimization, and index creation for vector types such as Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW). For more information, see Vector assist overview. For AlloyDB for PostgreSQL instances running PostgreSQL 17 and later, the maximum supported value for num_leaves when building ScaNN vector indexes is increased from 30,000,000 to 104,857,600. For more information, see Create a ScaNN index and ScaNN index reference. You can use the external_search_fdw extension to connect to external search clusters and query their data directly from your database using the following search sources: Elasticsearch Solr OpenSearch AlloyDB supports the rum extension for high-performance full-text search operations on PostgreSQL 17 and earlier. The rum extension extends standard GIN indexes by storing positional information directly in the index, letting you perform faster phrase searches and relevance ranking without accessing the table data. For more information, see Create and manage a RUM index.
title: The following AlloyDB AI and vector search features and improvements are generally available (GA): The alloydb_scann extension supports four-level tree (4LT) ScaNN vector indexes on PostgreSQL 17 and later, providing support for tables with up to 10 billion vector rows.

label: Preview
summary: The following AlloyDB AI functions and improvements are available in Preview: The ai.extract function lets you extract structured data from unstructured text directly within your database queries without needing external extraction pipelines. For more information, see Extract structured data. The ai.classify function lets you categorize unstructured text into predefined labels directly within your database queries. For more information, see Classify text. Parameter names and signatures for AI query engine functions (ai.analyze_sentiment, ai.summarize, and ai.agg_summarize) are updated. For more information, see Model endpoint reference. The prompt and prompts parameters are renamed to input and inputs in scalar and batch functions respectively. An optional additional_instructions parameter is added to ai.summarize and ai.agg_summarize to provide custom instructions to guide summary formatting, length, and tone. In cursor-based versions of ai.analyze_sentiment and ai.summarize, the prompt parameter is removed. ai.agg_summarize supports multiple positional signatures, including passing optional additional instructions and specifying model IDs.
title: The following AlloyDB AI functions and improvements are available in Preview: The ai.extract function lets you extract structured data from unstructured text directly within your database queries without needing external extraction pipelines.

Write endpoints simplify database connection management by providing a stable domain name service (DNS) name for your applications, decoupling them from instance IP addresses. During disaster recovery switchovers or failovers, AlloyDB automatically updates the endpoint to point to the new primary instance. For more information, see Manage database connections with write endpoints.

Cross-region failover is supported only for topologies with a single primary cluster and a single secondary cluster. For more information, see About cross-region replication and Work with cross-region replication.
title: AlloyDB now supports cross-region failover in Preview.

summary: Index prefetch is generally available (GA) and enabled by default for AlloyDB and AlloyDB Omni instances that run PostgreSQL 17 and later. Index prefetch speeds up B-tree index range scans by reading upcoming index and table pages in parallel into the local SSD cache, reducing query wait time for storage I/O without reducing PostgreSQL shared buffers. You don't need to configure flags, rebuild indexes, or modify applications or SQL queries to use prefetching. For more information, see Index prefetch overview.
title: Index prefetch is generally available (GA) and enabled by default for AlloyDB and AlloyDB Omni instances that run PostgreSQL 17 and later.

This integration allows you to combine the capabilities of AlloyDB with Elasticsearch for advanced search scenarios. For more information, see Access Elasticsearch data from AlloyDB.
title: External search with AlloyDB now supports Elasticsearch in Preview.

label: Preview
summary: The following AlloyDB AI function capabilities are available in Preview: You can now use AI function acceleration and the new AI Function Apply node to run faster queries with AI functions. This feature optimizes the execution of SQL queries that use the ai.if and ai.rank functions in PostgreSQL 17. For more information, see Accelerate performance for queries with AI functions. You can now use optimized AI functions to accelerate your AI queries while reducing operational costs. By training a smaller, faster proxy model on a sample of your data, AlloyDB can process most AI queries locally and only fall back to a remote LLM when necessary. For more information, see Accelerate queries using optimized functions. You can now use the sentiment analysis and summarization functions. These functions let you process and analyze unstructured data directly in your database: ai.analyze_sentiment: classifies the emotional tone of text as positive, negative, or neutral, helping you analyze real-time customer feedback from thousands of raw, unstructured product reviews. ai.summarize: condenses lengthy text into its essential information. Use this to extract key decisions and action items from sources like meeting transcripts or technical documentation. ai.agg_summarize: an aggregate function that processes multiple rows in a column to generate a single, unified summary for a group. For instance, you can summarize all reviews for a specific seller using a GROUP BY clause. For more information, see Evaluate sentiment and Summarize content.
title: The following AlloyDB AI function capabilities are available in Preview: You can now use AI function acceleration and the new AI Function Apply node to run faster queries with AI functions.

label: GA
summary: Adaptive filtering from inline filtering to pre-filtering is now generally available (GA). With AlloyDB AI, you can use adaptive filtering to optimize filtered vector searches. This feature enables the query optimizer to use cost-based analysis to dynamically choose the most efficient filtering strategy—either inline filtering or pre-filtering—based on real-time data distributions. This improves filtered vector search performance without requiring manual tuning or intervention. Note that the feature adaptive filtering from pre-filtering to inline filtering is still in Preview. For more information, see Understand adaptive filtering in AlloyDB AI.
title: Adaptive filtering from inline filtering to pre-filtering is now generally available (GA).

label: Preview
summary: The following vector search improvements are now available in Preview: AlloyDB now supports Vector assist. Vector assist is an AlloyDB extension that simplifies the deployment and management of your AlloyDB vector workloads. It helps you set up production-ready vector search capabilities, such as embedding generation, query optimization, and index creation for vector types like HNSW. For more information about vector assist, how it works, and its limitations, see Vector assist overview. You can now defer ScaNN index creation on an empty table or a table with insufficient rows until the table has sufficient data. For more information, see Create a ScaNN index. The alloydb_scann extension now supports four-level tree indexes, providing support for tables with up to 10 billion vector rows. For more information, see Four-level ScaNN tree indexes.
title: The following vector search improvements are now available in Preview: AlloyDB now supports Vector assist.

label: GA
summary: The alloydb_scann extension is updated to include the following vector search improvements. These features are generally available (GA): By default, new ScaNN vector index builds are automatically tuned. Manually-tuned indexes can be converted to automatically-tuned indexes. For more information, see Create a ScaNN index. You can now automatically maintain your ScaNN vector indexes. AlloyDB incrementally manages your index such that when your dataset grows, AlloyDB updates centroids and splits large outlier partitions to provide better QPS and search results. For more information, see Maintain indexes automatically.
title: The alloydb_scann extension is updated to include the following vector search improvements.
